Sites are greedy-optimal placements: each school is put where it covers the most children not already within reach of a recorded school, ranked by children covered.

Rural sites only. Candidate locations whose catchment averages more than 300 inhabitants per km² (the GHSL urban threshold) are excluded. A dense area with no school in the registry is nearly always a gap in the registry rather than a real shortage of schools, and ranking by coverage pulls hard toward exactly those places — before this restriction the top site was central Kampala.

Coverage percentages compare our extract against independent ministry counts. Where coverage is low, treat sites as indicative of underserved regions rather than as verified locations, and check against local records before committing funds.

Source: Crawfurd et al. (2025), from national EMIS registries and WorldPop grids.
